gemini-3.7-flash._price_recheck_2026_09_02: CHRONICLE OF A DOUBLE FLIP — read this before trusting any single reader on this page. (1) 2026-09-02 morning: WebFetch + one reviewer said prices doubled → CRITICAL alarm. (2) Same day: jina read_url x3 returned '$0.375 through December 31, 2026. $0.75 starting January 1, 2027' and the alarm was 'refuted' as summariser collapse. (3) Same day, cheap panel: THREE channels opened the page live and read Standard $0.75->$1.50, Batch $0.375->$0.75. The jina passages were REAL page text but were the BATCH rows — extractive passages arrive without section headings, the reranker returns whichever rows match the question, and attributing them to 'Standard' by table order was the error. RULE: a heading-less extractive passage cannot be attributed to a row label; for load-bearing prices require two independent TRANSPORTS reading the LABELLED row, and prefer a machine-readable reseller catalogue as tie-breaker (OR retailed 0.75 sync all along).

context_caching._the_trap: Storage bills $0.50 per 1M tokens PER HOUR. A 93,442-token cache costs $0.0467/hour to hold - leave one up for a day and it costs more than the batch it was meant to cheapen. CREATE, USE, DELETE. Always delete in a finally block; the TTL is only a backstop for when the delete itself fails.
context_caching._unverifiable_from_here: Whether the cached rate STACKS with the batch 50% discount is NOT determinable from this side, because Google returns no cost field. Cached input is $0.0375/M against batch input $0.1875/M either way, so the saving is real; only its exact size is open. Confirm in the Google billing console.

openrouter._flex_finding_2026_09_02: REFINED BY THE PANEL same day. (1) The /models catalogue has ZERO :flex slugs — true. (2) BUT /api/v1/models/{id}/endpoints carries PROVIDER TAGS with flex prices: 'openai/flex' $1/$5 on sol-pro, $1.25/$7.5 on gpt-5.4, $2.5/$15 on gpt-5.5; 'google-ai-studio/flex' $0.375/$1.875 on flash (grokbuild opened all four, 2026-09-02). So the discount PATH exists as endpoint tags, not slug variants — a safeguard checking slug suffixes would refuse a working discount. (3) Per OR service-tiers docs: service_tier:'flex' restricts routing to flex endpoints; capacity-miss ERRORS (no fallback); an EMPTY flex pool routes 'normally at standard rates' silently — the documented mechanism behind Probe D billing standard. FIX: pin provider.only to the flex-tagged endpoint AND verify by usage.cost meter; echo and HTTP 200 prove nothing. Probe D (08-23) remains the last METER on this path and it read standard.
openrouter._web_fee_note: Web fees are per-query, identical on sync and :batch (batch discounts tokens, never search — docs/batch-api-verified-2026-08-16.md section 2).
